newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down on long liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down across the board on Friday on long liquidation from retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded July 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,131 yuan ($378) per tonne, losing 36 yuan. It opened at 3,140 and hit a high of 3,300 yuan per tonne.
September fell 35 to 3,210, November 20 to 3,220, the January 1998 contract nine to 3,160, March two to 3,128 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 36,200 tonnes from 28,100 tonnes.
Soybeans opened lower and moved little for most of the session, traders said.

"Many investors liquidated their long positions today due to a lack of confidence in where the market is going," one trader said. "The domestic stock market are attracting a lot of the hot money away from soybeans."
Traders said they expected soybeans to maintain their downward trend in the next few days if there is no positive news.
